newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dlr ends at 8-yr low as US dlr firms abroad.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dlr ends at 8-yr low as US dlr firms abroad.

text.p: The slowly depreciating Taiwan dollar eased to yet another eight-year low close against its U.S. counterpart on Monday, reflecting the U.S. unit's strength against the mark and yen, dealers said.
The local dollar dipped as low as T$27.975 before recovering mildly to end at T$27.972 against Saturday's T$27.952 close.
Monday's finish surpassed an eight-year low of T$27.955 set on Friday.
The local unit has not closed lower since finishing at T$28.03 on January 7, 1989.
"Overseas, the U.S. dollar is strong against both the mark and the yen, so investors are testing the Taiwan dollar's downside support," said one dealer.
Dealers said they saw central bank intervention that clearly braked the slide at T$27.975, but noted that the bank did not appear to be trying to reverse the slow downtrend.
"The central bank did enter to smooth the Taiwan dollar depreciation, but I am surprised it did not push it up heavily before the close," one dealer said.
Dealers said Monday's U.S. dollar demand was mainly commercial and that speculative pressure was not heavy.
"Maybe because speculation was not heavy and since the depreciation was reflecting the overseas trend, the central bank did not vigorously defend the local dollar," a dealer said.
She said many investors had been expecting central bank intervention, hoping to buy comparatively cheap U.S. dollars if the central bank tried to push up the Taiwan dollar.
This strategy of speculating against the central bank's resolve had been less than successful as the intervention has not been predictably consistent.
"The central bank has moved smartly -- sometimes defending the currency vigorously, sometimes letting it move comparatively freely," she said.
"It's hard to predict which way it will move."

Dealers said they expected the local currency to slip further to test a 15-month intraday support at T$27.98 or even the more momentous eight-year support of T$28 -- but not before the central bank is ready.
"The central bank likely will try to defend the T$27.98 support for a while before giving it up," the dealer said.
For Tuesday, a T$27.95-98 range was seen.
